high.title: July Stock Market Through the Eyes of a Billion-Dollar Foreign Fund Manager: "Horrible"
high.summary:
Pyn Elite Fund, one of the most prominent foreign funds invested in Vietnam, reported a -9.6% performance in July (as of July 22), while the VN-Index declined a steep 10.3% over the same period. Fund manager Petri Deryng described July as "Horrible July" — the worst monthly performance for the fund since inception and the heaviest loss month since October 2023. Deryng expressed surprise at the market's weakness given strong Q1 corporate earnings growth and robust Vietnamese macroeconomic momentum in H1 2026. He noted that investor caution and declining prices have fueled concerns, without providing further detail in the excerpt. **Market implications:** A 10%+ decline in the VN-Index within a single month signals significant deterioration in risk sentiment toward Vietnamese equities. For international fund managers, this raises key questions about foreign capital outflows from the equity market, potential pressure on VND from foreign investor repatriation, and broader risk appetite toward Vietnamese assets. Watch for whether foreign net selling on HoSE accelerates and whether this spills into the government bond market via spread widening.

---

high.title: VN-Index May See Another "Shakeout" Before Targeting 1,800 Points — Many Stocks at Rare Valuation Levels with P/E of Only 4-8x
high.summary:
As of July 22, 2026, the VN-Index stood at 1,668 points with total market capitalization of approximately USD 382 billion, equivalent to ~74% of 2025 GDP. Headline valuation metrics are P/E 12.09x, P/B 1.81x, and P/S 1.44x. Critically, the Vingroup conglomerate alone accounts for ~USD 91 billion in market cap; stripping this out leaves the broader market at P/E 10.37x and P/B 1.53x — levels that SHS Securities notes are comparable to prior crisis-era market bottoms.

SHS warns that a further "shakeout" (technical correction/flush) may still occur before the market can sustainably rally toward the 1,800-point target. A notable risk factor flagged is that the ratio of margin lending to market capitalization is currently at a very high level, distinguishing the current environment from previous bottoming phases and heightening downside volatility risk.

high.title: Banks Aggressively Issuing Certificates of Deposit: Some Double Issuance Volume in 6 Months
high.summary: Vietnamese commercial banks are significantly ramping up Certificate of Deposit (CD) issuance amid intensifying competition for funding, according to Q2/2026 financial reports. ACB leads the headline figures, with total CD outstanding reaching VND 160,355 billion at end-June 2026 — a striking **98% increase** from year-start. Within that, short-term CDs (under 1 year) rose 42% to over VND 104 trillion, while 1–2 year CDs surged **6.5x** to VND 36,000 billion. Banks are cited as using this instrument to build medium-to-long-term funding bases to support accelerating credit growth. The trend signals that banks are facing structural funding pressure, likely pushing up the cost of liabilities across the sector.

high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates on July 28 at Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank...
high.summary: Vietnam's deposit rate landscape showed notable divergence on July 28. BaoViet Bank cut rates across multiple tenors: 6-month and 9-month rates trimmed from 6.6% to 6.4% p.a., while 12-month and 18-month tenors were reduced from 6.7% to 6.5% p.a. This dovish move contrasts sharply with ACB, which remains the market leader after aggressively raising rates last week — currently offering 7.8% p.a. for 12-month deposits, 7.7% for 9-month, and 7.6% for 6-month. Saigonbank (7.2%) and Bac A Bank (7.1%) follow, with MBV, VCBNeo, VIB, and PGBank all at the 7.0% threshold for 12-month tenors — bringing the total number of banks at or above 7% p.a. to seven institutions. Just below, LPBank, BVBank, and OCB are clustered at 6.9% p.a.

high.title: Vietnamese Stock Investors "Hold Their Breath" Awaiting Critical Fed Decision
high.summary:
The Vietnamese investment community is closely watching the U.S. Federal Reserve's two-day policy meeting concluding on July 29, 2026, amid a sharp correction in the VN-Index, which has shed over 200 points from its recent peak. According to Nguyen The Minh, Head of Investment Banking at An Binh Securities (ABS), U.S. 10-year Treasury yields remain elevated near their highest levels since 2025, creating headwinds for emerging market assets including Vietnamese equities and bonds. Notably, this Fed meeting is characterized by unusual uncertainty — unlike prior meetings, investors have few clear forward signals on the outcome. A growing number of major financial institutions now assign a non-trivial probability to a rate hike in July, citing surging oil prices and geopolitical tensions. **For VND and bond traders:** A Fed rate hike or a hawkish hold would likely pressure VND through stronger USD dynamics, potentially forcing SBV to intervene in the FX market and could push Vietnamese government bond yields higher as foreign capital re-prices EM risk. This is the single most important macro catalyst to watch this week.

---

medium.title: Securities Brokerages "Starving" — Q2 2026 Brokerage Revenue Collapses
medium.summary: Aggregate brokerage revenue across Vietnamese securities firms fell to approximately VND 3,600 billion in Q2 2026, down 27% quarter-on-quarter and 5% year-on-year — the lowest level since Q1 2025 and barely half the ~VND 7,000 billion peak recorded in Q3 2025. More concerning, gross profit for the sector collapsed 63% QoQ to around VND 400 billion, with gross margins falling to ~11% from 22% in Q1 2026, one of the lowest readings since 2023. The article attributes the squeeze to both lower market liquidity and structural shifts in securities business models. This data corroborates the VN-Index weakness flagged in the Pyn Elite Fund article and suggests a sustained deterioration in equity market activity rather than a short-term blip. For bond and FX investors, weakening capital market intermediation activity could dampen risk appetite more broadly and reduce domestic demand for financial assets.

medium.title: Vietnam's Neighboring Country China Imports 173 Tonnes of Gold in June — Highest in Over Two Years
medium.summary: China imported approximately 173 tonnes of gold in June 2026, up from 163 tonnes in May, marking the third consecutive monthly increase and the highest level since March 2024. The surge was driven by a combination of gold price pullbacks, a stronger CNY improving domestic purchasing power, and Chinese commercial banks restocking inventories to meet retail gold demand and gold accumulation program needs. While this article is China-focused, it carries indirect relevance for Vietnam's FX and gold market dynamics: elevated regional gold demand historically supports gold smuggling pressures and unofficial gold premiums in Vietnam, which can exert demand on USD in the parallel FX market. The SBV has previously intervened in gold markets precisely to address such distortions. Watch for any SBV commentary on domestic gold premiums in response to elevated regional demand.

medium.title: H1 2026 Business Results Update for 15 Banks: VIB, VietABank, VPBank, Techcombank, and Others
medium.summary: A sector-wide H1 2026 earnings snapshot across 15 Vietnamese commercial banks reveals a mixed picture. VIB reported pre-tax profit of VND 5,180 billion, up 3% year-on-year, with total assets exceeding VND 580 trillion (+4% YTD) and credit growth of 4%. VietABank posted stronger momentum with pre-tax profit of VND 826 billion, up 15.7% YoY, supported by 10% loan growth and 11.2% deposit growth. Notably, Saigonbank recorded a pre-tax loss of VND 40 billion in Q2 2026 (vs. a VND 76.4 billion profit in Q2 2025), with cumulative H1 profit collapsing 72.4% YoY to just VND 48 billion, signaling acute stress at the smaller end of the banking spectrum. For bond and equity investors, the divergence between mid-tier and smaller banks warrants attention — moderate credit growth across the system suggests the SBV's accommodative stance is transmitting unevenly. Saigonbank's loss raises asset quality concerns. Watch for non-performing loan disclosures and provisioning trends in the upcoming full quarterly filings.

medium.title: LPBank Shares Surge After New Shareholder List Disclosed — Pham Nhat Vuong Connection Revealed
medium.summary: LPBank's shares (ticker: LPB) hit the daily upper price limit of VND 56,000 on July 27, driven by the disclosure of a new major shareholder — Ms. Pham Thu Huong — who holds 148.3 million shares (4.965% of charter capital). Crucially, LPBank confirmed that Ms. Huong is a related party to billionaire Pham Nhat Vuong (founder of Vingroup), who separately holds 4.894% of LPB. Combined, the two directly control over 294.5 million shares (~9.86% of charter capital). This is a relevant development for equity investors tracking Vietnamese banking sector ownership concentration and potential strategic shifts at LPBank. The Vingroup connection may signal longer-term strategic interest in the bank. Monitor for any regulatory scrutiny around related-party ownership thresholds under SBV rules, as combined stakes approaching 10% could attract supervisory attention.

medium.title: H1 2026 Results of 13 Banks: 3 Report Negative Growth, One Bank's Profit Jumps 5x
medium.summary:
Vietnam's banking sector is showing sharp earnings divergence in H1 2026. On the negative side, **Saigonbank** reported a pre-tax loss of VND 40 billion in Q2 2026 (vs. VND 76.4 billion profit in Q2 2025), with cumulative H1 pre-tax profit collapsing 72.4% YoY to just VND 48 billion. Customer deposits fell 4.26% YTD, a notable liability-side deterioration. **Eximbank** fared no better, with H1 pre-tax profit estimated at VND 730 billion — a steep 51% YoY decline, completing only 48% of its full-year target. Total assets stood at VND 266,500 billion at end-Q2. The widening profit bifurcation across the sector has implications for credit growth momentum, provisioning pressure, and the trajectory of lending rates. Banks under earnings stress may tighten credit standards or resist passing on any future SBV rate cuts. For bond investors, deteriorating bank profitability could reduce appetite for government bond purchases at current yield levels. Watch for any SBV supervisory response to weaker institutions and whether NPL disclosures emerge alongside these results.

---

medium.title: Vietnam's Neighboring Country (China) Massively Imports 173 Tonnes of Gold in June — Highest in Over 2 Years
medium.summary: China's gold imports surged to **173 tonnes in June 2026**, up from 163 tonnes in May, marking the **third consecutive month of increase** and the highest reading since March 2024. The uptick was driven by gold price corrections creating buy-the-dip opportunities, a stronger CNY improving domestic purchasing power, and Chinese commercial banks restocking inventories to meet retail demand including gold accumulation programs. Analyst Zijie Wu of Jinrui Futures highlighted that banks needed to build buffer inventory to handle potential demand spikes. While this article focuses on China, it carries indirect relevance for Vietnam: strong regional gold demand can influence **domestic Vietnamese gold prices** and the SBV's gold market management posture, as Vietnam's gold market remains sensitive to regional price dynamics and import quota policies. Elevated gold demand regionally could also modestly affect broader USD/Asian currency dynamics.

medium.title: Gold Bar and Plain Gold Ring Prices on the Afternoon of July 28 at Bao Tin Minh Chau, Bao Tin Manh Hai, DOJI, PNJ, SJC...
medium.summary:
Domestic gold prices declined notably through the afternoon session of July 28, with major retailers SJC, PNJ, DOJI, Bao Tin Minh Chau, and Bao Tin Manh Hai all marking prices lower. Gold bar prices settled in a range of VND 137.5–141.5 million/tael by afternoon, down VND 1.5 million/tael from the morning open. Mi Hong jewelry store saw a sharper decline of VND 2 million/tael on the buy side. Plain 9999 gold rings also fell, with prices ranging from VND 136.2–142.5 million/tael depending on retailer. The morning opening had been VND 139.0–143.0 million/tael for gold bars across major dealers. While domestic gold pricing is primarily a retail market indicator, significant moves in gold premiums over international spot prices can reflect VND liquidity conditions and domestic safe-haven demand — both relevant secondary indicators for FX and monetary policy watchers.
